summary: Suppressed stream kickoff and elevated TTFB on chat completions after hybrid runtime/model handoff
description:
Issue summary: Since the hybrid-runtime 2.0 rolling handoff and model pin update on 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC, Wavefront customers report significantly delayed Time-To-First-Token (TTFB) for chat completion requests. Impact: multiple chat sessions observe a 1.2–3.5s increase in initial token latency; streaming responses sometimes do not start and eventually time out at the client (upstream 30s timeout).

Observed behaviour appears concentrated on sessions routed to the new runtime variant after the model handoff. Errors are intermittent but reproducible for a subset of request patterns that include system prompt + short user messages and stream=true.

Impact: Production latency SLA breaches for customer Wavefront (dedicated pool).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Wavefront account api-key against production endpoint in us-west-2; 2) Send chat completion request with system prompt and a short user message, streaming enabled; 3) Observe response start time. Reproduce rate: ~20% of sessions routed to runtime-2.0 show delayed kickoff.

Note: Non-streaming (single-response) requests show milder TTFB increases but succeed more often.
logs: Sample trace IDs: 20260310-wf-1a23, 20260310-wf-1a24. Proxy logs show upstream backend selected: runtime-2.0/pool-47, kernel: quant-path-A. API gateway timings: backend_connect 120–450ms, backend_first_byte 1.3–3.8s. No 5xx in gateway; some 429s seen in proxy during brief autoscale events (2026-03-10T03:12Z). Refer to flamegraph snapshots: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/trace/wavefront-20260310. Error sample from client: "streaming did not begin before timeout"
comments: 2026-03-10 04:05 - Support (Ava): Notified Wavefront CS that we're investigating. Collected example request/response timings and trace IDs.

2026-03-10 05:30 - SRE (Ravi): Initial triage indicates a tail in first-byte after handoff; scheduler shows increased cold-starts on pool-47 (runtime-2.0). Opening INT ticket to correlate with autoscaler behavior.
2026-03-10 07:12 - Customer (Wavefront - Lina): Customers seeing token delays impacting UI — request urgent update. Provided additional traces and a repro script.
2026-03-11 02:00 - Infra (N. Gomez): Identified CPU contention on the router pod handling prefix-caching updates during handoff; GC spikes observed in the proxy sidecar around the same windows.

2026-03-12 10:42 - Eng (Ravi): Deployed temporary routing rule to prefer warm pools for Wavefront until root cause confirmed. Monitoring TTFB; initial improvement to median but tail persists for ~2% of sessions.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Hybrid runtime 2.0 introduced a kernel selection path that defers KV-cache priming until first token emission when certain prefix lengths are detected; combined with newly observed scheduling of workers causes additional latency.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler churn led to brief resource scarcity resulting in queueing at the per-pool scheduler. 429s during autoscale windows correlate with increased backend_first_byte.

Evidence: Flamegraphs show >200ms spent in select_kernel() and ~1.1s in cache_miss path for affected requests. Router pod logs show GC pauses of 400–700ms during the interval. No OOMs or 5xx errors recorded.
Repro notes: Reproduced in staging by forcing cold worker allocation for runtime-2.0 with the same model; adding a pre-warm patch to allocate KV cache eliminated the extra ~1.1s in controlled tests.
Related PR: runtime/pull/982 contains compiler change that defers cache priming for quant-path-A when sequence_length < 64 (intended to optimize steady-state throughput).
resolution:
Workaround applied: routing rule to prefer warm pools for Wavefront and a temporary throttle on rolling handoff. Engineering will revert the deferred-cache-priming micro-optimization for quant-path-A and land patch runtime/pull/992 with pre-warm hook. Planned permanent fix: add proactive KV-cache priming during handoff and add autoscaler hysteresis to reduce churn.

Follow-up actions: ship PR 992, run blue-green test in staging, monitor TTFB for 72h, and schedule postmortem on 2026-03-16. Communicated ETA to customer: incremental mitigation in 6 hours, full rollback/patch within 48 hours.
